analysis:
Only docs/developer/test.md was supplied (head_text lines 2706-3583). It is documentation for benchmark and test procedures. It changes no coordinator, provider or attestation code, so no runtime security behavior changed.

Relevant material is T-041 (prefix-cache SSD tier). Lines 3093-3136 describe the isolated-cache test controls: DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_CACHE_ALLOW_EPHEMERAL, DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_CACHE_TEST_ROOT and DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_CACHE_TEST_PERSISTENT_KEY. They also describe the persistent test namespace and access group. The text says the root override is ignored without the isolation opt-in, and that namespace use forbids ephemeral key fallback. These statements are consistent with T-041's HMAC-keyed names, SE-rooted KEK and cache-storage validation, and they do not loosen those mitigations.

The doc says the test seam does not isolate full HTTP provider attestation and that no key bytes are exported. Cache-off rows report no created key. The 30-minute TTL and disk-budget text at 3100-3117 and 3148-3155 is consistent with T-041. Benchmark artifacts retain raw token arrays, prompts and reports (lines 2905 and 3050-3056), so operators must keep them in owned directories. This is documentation guidance with no new code attack surface, and I raised no finding.

The doc references the sampling, logit, attention-packet and metadata diagnostics. Those are benchmark-only and are not described as shipped serving paths. The diff context is limited to doc text, so the source for the claimed controls was not reviewed.

For integration: if code in the same PR changes the cache env gates, namespace validation, TTL or the benchmark diagnostics, check them against these documented claims. No cross-file security conflicts are visible from this unit.
